text:
anya: Observed a weird oscillation in eu-west after we scale to zero. Traffic burst -> CA spins up 4 gpus, then within ~90s most pods finish, CA tears them down, then another burst comes and we pay cold-start latency twice. Logs attached from the autoscaler window.
sam.k: Ugh. Is this the same pattern where downscale unneeded time is 5m? I thought we set it higher for the EU pools.
anya: It was 5m on the eu-gpu-nodepool. Metrics show many short-lived batches (~1-2m). CA log: "scale down: node unneeded after 120s" — looks like our node drain logic plus pod termination grace is letting CA decide too fast.
leo: Short bursts mean we get cost + latency. Two quick ideas: 1) increase scale-down cooldown for gpu pools to 10m, 2) add small warm capacity per AZ (1 spare gpu node tainted for prewarm). Both have tradeoffs.
marta: For 1) CA flags to tweak: use --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m and --scale-down-unready-time=20m. Also enable --balance-similar-node-groups to avoid ripping out all nodes in one AZ.
sam.k: Example flags we should try on the K8s cluster-autoscaler:

```
--scale-down-enabled=true
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-down-unready-time=20m
--expander=random
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
```
leo: For 2) the warm node approach: create one small GPU node per AZ with taint `prewarmed=true:NoSchedule` and run a warmer daemonset that keeps a lightweight container with model artifacts and warmed caches. When real jobs come, they tolerate the taint and schedule quicker. Cost ~3-4% increase but huge latency win.
anya: Curious about implementing jitter on drains so we don't evict all across AZ at once. Right now CA tends to pick similar nodes and we see multi-AZ churn.
marta: We can add drain splay via a small controller that delays cordon/drain by random(30s-120s) per node, or use node-termination-handler style jitter. CA itself doesn't have drain jitter.
leo: Another angle: predictive scaler based on recent event windows — keep a sliding single-node buffer if burst rate > X per minute. Sounds like a rollout for Optimize team, but doable at infra level for now.
infra-bot: ALERT: eu-west-gpu-nodepool scaled from 0 -> 4 at 1934567923, scale-down initiated at 1934568005. CPU/GPU utilization: spikes then median 10% after 75s.
sam.k: Quick experiment plan: 1) bump --scale-down-unneeded-time to 10m for gpu pools, 2) provision 1 tainted prewarm node per AZ (on-demand), 3) add drain jitter controller to nodepool alpha for 48h. Rollback knob ready.
anya: I'll run the experiment tomorrow morning. If we see cost blowup we revert. Also let's keep telemetry: cold-start p90 and cost per inference per 24h.
leo: Also check AZ capacity constraints — eu-west sometimes has spot shortages causing longer startup. If warm nodes are spot, that defeats the purpose. Use on-demand for warmers.
marta: Noted. I'll update the CA config PR and add the drain-splay controller manifest. Ping me when you deploy the prewarm daemonset.
anya: Thanks all. Deploy plan: staging tomorrow 06:15 UTC, monitor 2h, then canary to prod if p90 latency drops without >5% cost increase. :thumbsup:
